editorial.headline: Soft Drinks, Without the Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 11053 covers non-alcoholic soft-drink manufacturing, open across business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record provided.
editorial.body:
KBLI 11053 is the manufacturing category for soft drinks: beverages without alcohol, excluding non-alcoholic beer and non-alcoholic wine. In practical terms, the record places here the production of flavored and/or sweetened non-alcoholic drinks such as lemonade, orangeade, cola, fruit-flavored drinks, milk-flavored drinks, coffee-flavored drinks, tea-flavored drinks, and tonic water. It also includes other non-alcoholic beverages such as soy-based drinks, drinks made from fruit nectar, and powdered soft drinks.

That scope matters because this is not merely a retail label or a bottling activity. The activity is the making of the drink itself: formulating, producing, and bringing a non-alcoholic beverage product into industrial form. The record also draws the outer edge of the category by excluding several adjacent activities, including fruit and vegetable juice production, milk-based beverage manufacturing, tea, coffee and mate products, alcoholic beverages, non-alcoholic wine, non-alcoholic beer, edible ice for consumption, and standalone bottling or labelling when that work is part of wholesale trade or performed on a fee or contract basis.

On registration scale, the record is unusually broad. KBLI 11053 is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, which means the activity is not reserved in the slim record for only a narrow size of operator. A small producer of powdered soft drinks and a larger manufacturer of carbonated or flavored beverages sit inside the same activity description, provided the real business activity remains the manufacture of the covered non-alcoholic drink products.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The activity is recorded as TERBUKA, and pma_max_asing is set at 100, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. The Bali picture is also not a moratorium block on this record: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked. So the honest reading is straightforward: a foreign-owned setup is nationally open, and the slim record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
